question: A dealer purchased a ceiling fan for ₹66,000. He allows a discount of 56% on its marked price and still gains 69%. Find the marked price of the ceiling fan.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the ratio relationship: **MP ÷ CP = (100 + Gain%) ÷ (100 − Discount%)**.

MP ÷ 66,000 = (100 + 69) ÷ (100 − 56) = 169 ÷ 44.

MP = (66,000 × 169) ÷ 44 = 1,500 × 169.

MP = 2,53,500.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2,53,500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given → **Cost Price (CP)** = ₹66,000, **Profit%** = 69%, **Discount%** = 56%.
Formulas: SP = CP × (100 + P%) ÷ 100 | MP = (SP × 100) ÷ (100 − D%).
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6e73792a5389675865337dd391cbcf130e7cc94fe677912ecf90c2043f92bb34.png] 
⇒ Calculate **Selling Price (SP)**: SP = 66,000 × (169 ÷ 100) = 660 × 169 = ₹1,11,540.
⇒ Calculate **Marked Price (MP)**: 1,11,540 = MP × (100 − 56) ÷ 100.
⇒ 1,11,540 = MP × 44 ÷ 100.
⇒ MP = (1,11,540 × 100) ÷ 44.
⇒ MP = 2,535 × 100 = ₹2,53,500.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2,53,500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Discount

The **Marked Price (MP)** is the price listed by the seller, and **Discount** is always calculated on this MP to arrive at the Selling Price.

CP-MP Relation

The direct formula **CP/MP = (100 − D%)/(100 + P%)** is a very efficient way to solve problems involving both discount and profit percentages.
